claim: For the three-state ferromagnetic Potts model with constant external field on the Cayley tree of order \(k=5\), use the notation of Bogachev--Rozikov and let \(\alpha_1(\theta)\) be their exceptional boundary field. For every \(3/2<\theta\le\sqrt{11}/2\), the source system (2.33) at \(\alpha=\alpha_1(\theta)\) has exactly one positive solution, namely \[(u,v)=((4\theta-2)/5,1).\] Equivalently, the source function \(K_1(v;\theta)\) has its unique global maximum on \(\mathscr V_1^+(\theta)\) at \(v=1\). Thus Conjecture 2.1 of arXiv:1903.11440 holds for the first previously unresolved order \(k=5\), closing the conjectural critical-boundary segment for that order. The proof does not address \(k\ge6\), nonconstant external fields, nonhomogeneous splitting states, or Gibbs measures outside the source reduction.
integrity: The proof is an exact algebraic reduction from the published definitions and reversible boundary-law equations. The accompanying polynomial checker verifies the stated identities exactly; no finite experiment is used as an infinite-domain proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to \(q=3\), \(k=5\), constant external field, and the completely homogeneous splitting-Gibbs-measure reduction.
No claim is made for \(k\ge6\), nonhomogeneous boundary laws, or Gibbs measures outside the source reduction.
title: Order-five uniqueness on the three-state Potts external-field boundary
